clips.text_en_c1: Treasury yields have gone into full-blown melt-up mode on /biz/ tonight, with the two-, ten-, and thirty-year tenors all grinding higher in lockstep. Basis points are climbing relentlessly; every time the Fed signals a cut, the market un-prices it within hours. Anons with duration exposure are being routed, while anyone who faded the dovish narrative earlier is sitting on a windfall. The tape is punishing the consensus trade, and sentiment has flipped from complacent to genuinely uneasy — a textbook case of the market reasserting its verdict over policymakers.
clips.text_en_c2: Treasury yields have detached from orthodoxy once again on /biz/, with the 2-, 10-, and 30-year tenors all grinding higher in lockstep. Each basis-point tick feels punitive, and the term premium, that elusive compensation for duration risk, has reasserted itself with a vengeance. The Fed's dovish pivot was repriced within hours, leaving anyone positioned for cuts nursing a bruised book. Anecdotally, the move has the unmistakable whiff of a yield melt-up: front-end bids vanish, long-end supply gets absorbed without protest, and the curve steepens in a manner that punishes precisely those who had leaned into duration. A chastening evening for the bulls.

clips.text_en_b2: Cramming for the FE exam tonight, and load path is the topic on the table. A vertical load travels from the slab into the beam, down through the column, into the footing, and finally dissipates into the soil. clips.text_en_c1: Working through load path concepts for the FE exam tonight, which strikes me as the single most exam-worthy topic in the entire syllabus. A vertical load enters the slab, transfers into the supporting beam, travels down through the column, disperses across the footing, and ultimately dissipates into the underlying soil — simple in principle, yet each transition demands its own capacity check. Reinforced concrete and structural steel achieve this through fundamentally different mechanisms: RC relies on composite action between rebar and concrete, whereas steel depends on connection detailing and carefully proportioned member sizes. The exam consistently rewards candidates who can trace the path methodically and verify every link.
clips.text_en_c2: Spent the evening buried in FE preparation, untangling the load path that carries a vertical reaction from slab to soil. The trajectory is deceptively linear: slab to beam, beam to column, column to footing, footing to founding stratum, each interface demanding its own capacity check. Reinforced concrete and structural steel negotiate this descent through entirely different idioms; RC relies upon composite action between rebar and concrete, whereas steel depends upon connection detailing, member proportions, and the precise distribution of plastic hinges at ultimate limit state. The exam, with characteristic malice, rewards those who can trace the path fluently and interrogate each link without losing the thread.
